prompt:
A plan for a software change ends with a table of risks. Decide, for each reference problem, whether any row of the table addresses the same underlying problem (names it as a risk or mitigates it specifically), even if worded differently.

Change request: Make the session middleware's cookie Secure and SameSite=Strict by default.

Reference problems:
1. In starlette/testclient.py, TestClient defaults to baseurl="http://testserver". Because HTTPX does not transmit Secure cookies over insecure HTTP connections, enabling Secure by default will break the majority of existing test cases in tests/middleware/testsession.py that rely on sessions persisting across requests.
2. Applications running in local development or test environments over plain HTTP (such as http://127.0.0.1:8000 or non-TLS containers) will fail to persist sessions because browsers drop Secure cookies on unencrypted origins. Developers would encounter broken session behavior out of the box without clear diagnostic errors.
3. Setting SameSite=Strict by default prevents browsers from sending the session cookie on top-level cross-site GET navigations, such as following an external link or opening a bookmark. Users navigating to the application from external sites will appear unauthenticated on their initial landing page until an internal navigation occurs.
4. Authentication workflows that rely on third-party redirects—such as OAuth2 callbacks, OpenID Connect logins, or SAML identity provider flows—will break because incoming redirects will not carry the session cookie under SameSite=Strict. This will cause state parameter validation failures and loss of pre-authenticated session context.
5. SessionMiddleware handles scope["type"] == "websocket", extracting cookies during the initial connection handshake. Marking the cookie Secure by default will block browsers from sending the session cookie over unencrypted WebSocket connections (ws://), breaking WebSocket endpoints during local development or in non-TLS environments.
6. SessionMiddleware supports partitioned cookies for embedded contexts (partitioned: bool = False), which explicitly requires samesite="none" and HTTPS as documented in docs/middleware.md. Defaulting to SameSite=Strict will silently break embedded or iframe use cases unless developers explicitly override both parameters.
7. docs/middleware.md explicitly instructs users that httpsonly defaults to False and samesite defaults to 'lax', with specific recommendations for production configuration. Modifying these defaults without synchronizing the documentation, release notes, and migration guides will cause user confusion and unexpected breaking changes for downstream frameworks like FastAPI.
8. Cookie‑clearing inconsistencies – The code that clears a session (elif session.modified and not initialsessionwasempty) re‑uses self.securityflags. If the defaults are changed, stale cookies set with the old flag combination may remain, causing ambiguous session state after a logout.
9. Reduced flexibility for advanced users – The httpsonly flag becomes redundant, and developers who previously relied on toggling it to enable Secure only in production will lose that granular control, possibly requiring code changes elsewhere.

Rows of the risk table:
-  OAuth/SSO logins break   Login libraries keep their state check in `request.session`. The return trip from the identity provider is a cross-site navigation, so a Strict cookie isn't sent and the check fails   Explain in the docs and release note that `same_site="lax"` is needed for these flows  
-  Silent logout over plain http   The browser won't send a Secure cookie back over http, so the session looks empty on every request. No error is raised   Highlight the opt-out for http in the docs  
-  Large test fallout   The test client's default URL is `http://testserver`, so most session tests stop sending the cookie   Use an `https://` base URL in the affected tests  
-  Users' own test suites break   Downstream apps test with Starlette's default test client over http   Breaking-change note with a one-line fix  
-  Logged out when arriving from another site   With Strict, the first visit from an email or another site's link arrives without the cookie, so a logged-in user looks logged out   Document the trade-off; Lax remains an option  
-  Safari and localhost   Older Safari versions reject Secure cookies on `http://localhost`, unlike Chrome and Firefox   Mention local development in the docs  
-  Wrong version bump   This is a breaking default change in a minor-version line   Maintainers decide the release; label it clearly  
-  Duplicate PR   AI_POLICY.md bans contributors who open duplicate PRs   Search PRs, issues and discussions first  
-  Frameworks built on Starlette inherit it   FastAPI and others re-export `SessionMiddleware`, so their users get the change without warning   Clear release note; consider pinging the downstream projects  

Answer directly from the text above; do not run commands or use tools. Answer with JSON only, one key per reference number: {"1": true, "2": false, ...}
